section_titles: Recommendations for the treatment of transthyretin amyloidosis-cardiac amyloidosis
content.TTR_section_summary: TTR stabilization and reduction of its production are the basis of TTR-CA treatment. Liver and/or cardiac transplantation may be considered only in end-stage familial TTR-CA. Tafamidis reduced all-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalizations in biopsy-proven hereditary and wild-type TTR-CA, mainly in patients with NYHA class I and II at baseline; functional improvement occurred within 6 months, mortality decrease took nearly 2 years. Intravenous patisiran (siRNA) or subcutaneous inotersen (antisense oligonucleotide) against TTR may be considered for patients with combined hereditary TTR polyneuropathy and cardiac amyloidosis. Off-label diflunisal may be considered in wild-type TTR-CA in combination with a proton pump inhibitor.
content.iron_overload_summary: Iron overload results from hereditary haemochromatosis or repeated transfusions (eg, beta-thalassaemia). In iron overload the iron-binding capacity of transferrin is saturated and non-transferrin-bound iron enters cardiomyocytes through L-type calcium channels causing oxidative myocardial damage. Iron-induced complications (liver disease, endocrine abnormalities) contribute to cardiac deterioration leading to iron overload cardiomyopathy (restrictive or dilated phenotype). Myocardial iron deposition is quantified by CMR T2*; T2* values correlate with ventricular systolic function and predict iron-induced heart failure or arrhythmias. Prevention and treatment include iron chelators (deferoxamine, deferiprone, deferasirox) and intensified combined chelation therapy which may reverse established disease.
recommendations_table_text: Tafamidis is recommended in patients with genetic testing proven hereditary TTR-CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, cardiovascular hospitalization and mortality. (Class I, Level B)
Tafamidis is recommended in patients with wild-type TTR-CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, cardiovascular hospitalization and mortality. (Class I, Level B)

genes.context: TTR discussed throughout as the target of stabilization and gene-silencing therapies (tafamidis, patisiran, inotersen); references to hereditary and wild-type TTR cardiac amyloidosis and TTR-polyneuropathy, and to transplantation in end-stage familial disease.
